# main's own `#hit` keeps its id, and badge's is renamed so that `c.hit` finds
# main's. A lowering diagnostic about badge's names it as the program wrote it.
# badge's handler writes a place reading its own parameter, which
# passHandleBlocks cannot raise to the site, so the branch is left as written
# and its call through `#hit` is refused.

! sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stderr '`hit.reset\(\)` calls a method of the node `#hit`'
! stderr '__own'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

component counter node {
    var n = 0
    func reset() {
        n = 0
    }
    button(text="n{n}", @click { n = n + 1 })
}

component badge node {
    var open = true
    var marks = [0, 0]
    vbox {
        if open {
            counter #hit
            checkbox(label="reset", @change(on) {
                marks[on ? 1 : 0] = 1
                hit.reset()
            })
        }
    }
}

component main node {
    var mh = 0
    vbox {
        button #hit(text="m{mh}", @click { mh = mh + 1 })
        badge
    }
}

func testHit(t Test, c main) {
    c.hit.click()
    t.assert(c.mh == 1)
}

window {
    main
}
